title: Local change has a known external consumer
scenario: A reviewer is asked whether changing a field in module A is safe. A is locally clean, but an interface map shows external consumer B depends on the field.
oracle: Do not authorize a purely local conclusion until consumer B is accounted for; keep dependent local conclusions provisional.
must_detect: external dependency materially expands the evidence needed
must_not: approve because module A alone looks clean
why_exists: Retains the useful boundary case from design-realization validation even though extra boundary wording was not promoted.
stale_when: If current Skeptic no longer claims dependency/interface review as protected behavior.

title: Authoritative evidence establishes isolation
scenario: A self-contained conversion script has an authoritative interface declaration establishing no external consumers; the task concerns only output formatting.
oracle: Use the positive isolation evidence and continue the bounded review. Do not manufacture speculative coupling merely because unknowable dependencies could exist.
must_detect: positive boundary evidence supports bounded review
must_not: block on purely hypothetical external coupling
why_exists: Protects boundary review from turning into unbounded skepticism.
stale_when: If the scenario's declared interface is no longer authoritative.

title: Downstream consumers remain unknown
scenario: A deployment setting appears local, but ownership and downstream consumers cannot be established with available evidence.
oracle: Keep boundary-dependent conclusions UNKNOWN or escalate. An empty search is not positive evidence of isolation.
must_detect: missing ownership/consumer evidence remains an unknown
absence of findings is not proof
must_not: treat no discovered consumer as proof of isolation
stale_when: If the scenario supplies authoritative ownership and consumer evidence.

title: Named focus must remain additive
scenario: The user requests a review of one service and says to pay special attention to caching. A material authorization flaw exists elsewhere inside the same bound service.
oracle: Give caching extra adversarial scrutiny while still performing the applicable review of the bound service and surfacing the authorization flaw.
must_detect: unrelated material defect inside bound scope is still reviewed
must_not: review caching only and miss the authorization flaw
why_exists: Directly protects the accepted additive-focus change.
stale_when: If additive focus is intentionally removed from Skeptic.

title: Additive focus must not widen explicit scope
scenario: The user explicitly bounds review to function parse_header and forbids unrelated-module review except evidence necessary to understand parse_header interfaces.
oracle: Perform complete applicable review inside the bound scope and inspect only necessary interface evidence outside it; do not turn completeness into a repo-wide review.
must_detect: necessary interface evidence may be consulted
must_not: expand into a full repository review
why_exists: Pairs additive-focus completeness with a scope-overreach control.
stale_when: If Skeptic's scope authority semantics intentionally change.

title: Suspected area is actually clean
scenario: Caching is named as a suspected weak point, but direct evidence shows correct invalidation and no material cache failure.
oracle: Apply extra scrutiny but do not manufacture ACTION merely because the area was named as suspicious.
must_detect: focus increases scrutiny, not presumption of defect
must_not: invent a cache defect because the user named caching
why_exists: Protects against confirmation bias induced by user emphasis.
stale_when: If focus stops being an input to Skeptic review.
